examples.en: I followed the guard to the visiting room.
My uncle works as a correctional officer at a prison.
Correctional officers make rounds at night too.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 교도관 역할을 맡은 배우가 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The actor who played the prison guard in the drama was cool.
To become a correctional officer, you have to take an exam.
I asked the guard, and he said visits are only on weekdays.

explain: 예전에는 '간수'라고 불렀지만 지금은 거의 쓰지 않고 '교도관'이라고 해요. 경찰은 범인을 잡고, 교도관은 형을 받은 사람이 지내는 곳을 지키는 일을 해요. 교도소 이야기에서 가장 먼저 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I want to become a prison guard later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 목표로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a career goal.

phrases.en: My aunt has worked as a prison guard for ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 직업을 말할 때 '-(으)로 일하다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-(으)로 일하다' to talk about one's current job.
phrases.en_equiv: to work as a prison guard

phrases.en: I greeted the prison guard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부르거나 높여서 말할 때 '-님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-님' when addressing or showing respect to the person.

explain_en: In the past people called them '간수', but that is hardly used now and they are called '교도관'. The police catch criminals, while a '교도관' looks after the place where people serving a sentence stay. It is the first word you meet in talk about prisons.

examples.en: A representative from each class attended the meeting.

examples.ko: 계약서에는 회사 대표자의 이름을 적어야 해요.
examples.en: You have to write the company representative's name on the contract.
Who is the representative of our group?

examples.ko: 학생 대표자를 뽑는 투표가 내일 있어요.
examples.en: The vote to choose a student representative is tomorrow.
Only the representatives, please go in first.
My father attended as the family representative.

explain: '대표자'는 여러 사람을 대신해 나서는 사람이에요. '대표'는 사람과 상징 모두에 쓰고, '대표자'는 사람에게만 써요. 회사에서는 사장을 '대표자'나 '대표'라고도 불러요.

phrases.en: I was chosen as our class representative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람 중에서 대표가 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is chosen from many to represent them.

phrases.en: The student representatives talked with the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 모임의 대표인지 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the group name before it to show whom they represent.

phrases.example: 우리 반 대표가 앞에 나와서 발표해요.
phrases.en: Our class representative comes to the front and presents.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대표자'보다 짧고 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than '대표자' and common in daily speech.

explain_en: Representative — one person chosen to speak for a group. 대표자 is a person who acts on behalf of many people. 대표 can refer to a person or a symbol, while 대표자 refers only to people. At companies the boss is also called 대표자 or 대표.

t90.ax: Who is the representative of our group?

examples.en: Who holds the patent for this technology?
He was designated a holder of intangible cultural heritage.
I met a world record holder in person.

examples.ko: 면허 보유자만 이 차를 운전할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only license holders can drive this car.
That company is the holder of many patents.
They give a discount to cardholders.

explain: '기록 보유자', '자격증 보유자'처럼 앞에 가진 것을 붙여 써요. 물건을 가진 평범한 주인은 '주인'이나 '소유자'라고 해요. 회사나 나라는 '보유 기업', '보유국'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 일은 자격증 보유자만 할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only certificate holders can do this job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 가진 것을 붙여 '무엇을 가진 사람'이라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put what they hold in front to mean 'a person who has X'.

phrases.en: That athlete is the world record holder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠에서 가장 좋은 기록을 가진 사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in sports for the person who holds the best record.

phrases.en: We sent a notice text to the holders.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 사람을 한꺼번에 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '들' refers to several holders at once.

explain_en: One who holds a record, title, or skill; official nuance. You put what someone holds in front, as in '기록 보유자' (record holder) or '자격증 보유자' (certificate holder). For an ordinary owner of an object, people say '주인' or '소유자'. For companies and countries, they say '보유 기업' and '보유국'.

t90.ax: They give a discount to cardholders.

examples.ko: 운전면허증 소지자만 이 차를 빌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only holders of a driver's license can rent this car.
Holders of this coupon get 10% off drinks.
The company said it gives preference to certificate holders.

examples.ko: 입장권 소지자는 이쪽 줄에 서 주세요.
examples.en: Ticket holders, please line up on this side.
Passport holders, please enter this way.
We give a gift to holders of the preferred card.

explain: 앞에 면허증, 쿠폰, 카드처럼 물건 이름을 붙여서 그것을 가진 사람이라는 뜻으로 써요. 안내문이나 공고에서 자주 보고, 대화에서는 '가진 사람'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요. '소지품', '소지하다'와 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 면허증 소지자는 줄을 서지 않고 들어가세요.
phrases.en: Licence holders can go in without waiting in line.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소지자' 앞에 물건 이름을 붙이는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pattern: an item name before 'holder'.

phrases.example: 이 카드 소지자는 박물관에 무료로 들어가요.
phrases.en: Holders of this card get into the museum for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카드를 가진 사람을 안내문 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in a notice-like tone for people who have a card.

phrases.example: 티켓을 가진 사람만 들어갈 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only people who have a ticket can enter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 '소지자'를 쉽게 풀어서 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, spoken way to say 'holder' in conversation.

explain_en: One who carries a ticket, coupon, or permit at hand. Put an item name before it, such as a license, coupon or card, to mean the person who has it. You often see it in notices and announcements, while in conversation people may say '가진 사람' instead. Learn it together with '소지품' and '소지하다'.

t90.ax: Passport holders, please enter this way.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 동호회 준회원이라서 투표를 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm still only an associate member of the club, so I can't vote.
For a month, you take part as an associate member.
Can associate members use the library too?
The joining fee for associate members is cheaper than for full members.
Next month I go from associate member to full member.
To become an associate member, you have to submit documents.

explain: '정회원'의 반대말로 짝지어 외우면 좋아요. '준-'은 정식은 아니지만 그에 가깝다는 느낌을 더해요. 권리가 일부 제한되는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I became an associate member of the club this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식 회원이 되기 전의 단계가 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means reaching the stage before becoming a full member.

phrases.en: I joined as an associate member first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 가입할 때 어떤 자격인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says what status you have when you first sign up.

phrases.en: I'll become a full member in three months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '정회원'과 짝으로 외워 두면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Good to learn as a pair with its opposite, 정회원.

explain_en: Learn it as the counterpart of '정회원' (full member). The prefix '준-' adds the sense of 'not fully official, but close'. Often some rights are limited.

examples.ko: 이 글은 특정인을 비난하려는 게 아니에요.
examples.en: This post isn't meant to blame any particular person.
It's unfair to give benefits only to certain individuals.
The news did not reveal the name of the person involved.

examples.ko: 이 문자는 특정인에게 보낸 게 아니에요.
examples.en: This message wasn't sent to a particular person.

examples.ko: 특정인이 정보를 독점하고 있다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a rumor that one person is monopolizing the information.

examples.ko: 회사는 특정인만 위한 규칙을 만들지 않아요.
examples.en: The company doesn't make rules just for one person.

explain: 뉴스나 공지문에서 이름을 말하지 않고 한 사람을 가리킬 때 써요. 반대로 여러 사람을 가리키면 '불특정 다수'라고 해요. 대화에서는 '어떤 사람'이라고 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 특정한 사람만 이 방에 들어갈 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only certain people can enter this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특정인'을 풀어서 말한 것으로 대화에서 더 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out version of 'teukjeongin' that is easier in conversation.

phrases.example: 어떤 사람이 문 앞에서 기다리고 있어요.
phrases.en: Someone is waiting at the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 이름을 말하지 않고 사람을 가리킬 때 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to refer to a person without a name in conversation.

phrases.example: 이 서비스는 특정인을 위한 게 아니에요.
phrases.en: This service isn't meant for a specific person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공지문이나 설명 글에서 자주 보이는 격식 있는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase often seen in notices and explanations.

explain_en: News and notices use it to point to one person without giving a name. The opposite idea is 불특정 다수 (an unspecified crowd). In conversation, people more often just say 어떤 사람.

examples.ko: 가격을 몰래 올린 회사에 과징금이 부과됐어요.
examples.en: A penalty fine was imposed on the company that secretly raised prices.
I heard they have to pay a penalty of several billion won.

examples.ko: 과징금이 너무 적어서 효과가 없다는 의견도 있어요.
examples.en: Some say the fine is too small to be effective.

examples.ko: 그 기업은 과징금에 불복해서 소송을 냈어요.
examples.en: The company refused to accept the fine and filed a lawsuit.

examples.ko: 개인정보를 유출한 업체가 과징금을 내게 됐어요.
examples.en: The company that leaked personal information has to pay a penalty fine.
The amount of penalty fines is increasing every year.

explain: 뉴스에서 '과징금 부과'처럼 자주 나오고, 주로 정부 기관이 기업에 물리는 돈이에요. 형사 처벌인 '벌금'과는 달라요. 교통 위반은 보통 '범칙금'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The Fair Trade Commission imposed a penalty surcharge on the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 돈을 물릴 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for an authority imposing the charge.

phrases.en: That company decided to pay the penalty surcharge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물게 된 쪽에서 돈을 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side that has to pay.

phrases.en: I saw the news about the penalty surcharge being imposed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스 제목이나 기사에서 명사처럼 짧게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short noun phrase typical of news headlines and articles.

explain_en: Surcharge imposed on businesses by authorities for violations or unfair profit (company, regulation) It appears in news as '과징금 부과', and it is money a government agency imposes, mainly on companies. It differs from '벌금', which is a criminal penalty. Traffic violations are usually called '범칙금'.

t90.ax: Some say the fine is too small to be effective.

examples.en: I paid a fine for driving while looking at my phone.
How much is the speeding fine on this road?
The fine notice came to my house.
You get a fine if you don't wear your seat belt.
You must pay the fine within the deadline.
I ran a light on my motorcycle and had to pay a fine.

explain: 주로 교통법규를 어겼을 때 내는 돈이에요. '범칙금을 내다/물다/부과받다'로 써요. 비슷한 '과태료', '벌금'이 있지만 제도가 서로 달라서 같은 말은 아니에요.

phrases.en: Can I pay the fine in cash?
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적으로 쓰는 말이에요. 돈을 낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic expression, meaning to pay the fine.

phrases.en: I ran a red light and had to pay a fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내다'보다 잘못 때문에 어쩔 수 없이 낸다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like paying unwillingly because of a mistake, compared with 내다.
phrases.en_equiv: to be made to pay a fine

phrases.en: If you speed, you get a fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙을 어기면 범칙금이 생긴다는 뜻으로 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say a fine will be issued if you break a rule.

explain_en: Fine paid by individuals for minor offenses like traffic violations (신호 위반) It is mainly the money you pay for breaking traffic rules, used as '범칙금을 내다/물다/부과받다'. There are similar words, '과태료' and '벌금', but they belong to different systems, so they are not the same thing.

t90.ax: The fine notice came to my house.

examples.en: This furniture is delivered fully assembled.

examples.ko: 조립 키트보다 완성품이 값이 더 비싸요.
examples.en: The finished product costs more than the assembly kit.
At the factory they pick out and inspect only the finished goods.

examples.ko: 아직 완성품이 나오지 않아서 기다리는 중이에요.
examples.en: The finished product hasn't come out yet, so I'm waiting.
Seeing the finished product, it looked much better than the blueprint.

examples.ko: 완성품은 한 달 뒤에 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can receive the finished product in a month.

explain: 부품이나 재료 상태가 아니라 다 만들어져서 바로 쓸 수 있는 물건을 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말로는 '반제품'이나 '조립 제품'이 있어요. 장난감, 가구, 프라모델 같은 물건을 살 때 자주 구별해요.

phrases.en: Assembly was hard, so I bought it already finished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조립 없이 바로 쓸 수 있는 상태로 산다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means buying it in a ready-to-use state with no assembly.
phrases.en_equiv: to buy it as a finished product

phrases.en: If you order, you receive the finished product in three days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배송이나 주문 상황에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in delivery or ordering situations.

phrases.en: A semi-finished product has to be assembled at the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완성품과 구별해서 아직 덜 만들어진 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Contrasted with 완성품, it refers to a product not yet completely made.

explain_en: It refers to a thing that is completely made and ready to use, not in parts or materials. Contrasting words include '반제품' (semi-finished goods) and assemble-it-yourself products. The distinction often matters when buying toys, furniture or model kits.

t90.ax: This furniture is delivered fully assembled.

examples.ko: 부모님께 집을 증여받을 때는 세금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: When you receive a house as a gift from your parents, you have to pay tax.

examples.ko: 증여 계약서를 쓰기 전에 변호사와 상담했어요.
examples.en: I consulted a lawyer before writing the gift contract.

examples.ko: 자녀에게 미리 증여를 하면 세금이 줄어드나요?
examples.en: Does the tax go down if you give to your children in advance?
How are gifting and inheritance different?

examples.ko: 할머니가 땅을 증여한 사실이 나중에 알려졌어요.
examples.en: It later became known that my grandmother had given away her land.

examples.ko: 이번 증여 때문에 형제들 사이가 안 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: Because of this gift of property, relations between the siblings got worse.

explain: 살아 있을 때 대가 없이 재산을 주는 것이고, 죽은 뒤에 물려주는 '상속'과 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 '물려주다', '주다'라고 하고, '증여'는 세금이나 법 이야기에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: If you receive a house as a gift, you have to pay gift tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증여를 받은 사람이 내는 세금이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The tax paid by the person who receives a gift of property.

phrases.example: 사전 증여를 하면 나중에 상속세를 줄일 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you give property in advance, you can reduce inheritance tax later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 죽기 전에 미리 재산을 주는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means giving property in advance, before one's death.

phrases.en: I received a small apartment from my parents as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재산을 받는 사람의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word used from the point of view of the person receiving the property.
phrases.en_equiv: to receive as a gift of property

explain_en: Legal term for transferring property to someone, often family. This means giving property without payment while the giver is alive, which differs from '상속' (inheritance after death). In daily talk people say '물려주다' or '주다', while '증여' appears mostly in talk about taxes and law.

t90.ax: How are gifting and inheritance different?

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 안 쓰는 가구를 처분해요.
examples.en: Before moving, I get rid of the furniture I don't use.

examples.ko: 오래된 차를 처분하고 새 차를 샀어요.
examples.en: I got rid of the old car and bought a new one.
I opened a shop with the money from selling my house.
Trash must be disposed of according to the rules.
We plan to sell off the stock cheaply.
I got rid of the books I didn't need all at once.

explain: '팔다'는 돈을 받고 넘기는 것이고, '버리다'는 그냥 내놓는 것이에요. '처분하다'는 팔거나 버려서 정리한다는 넓은 말이라 집, 차, 재고처럼 큰 물건에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I'm selling off my furniture cheaply because of the move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨리 없애려고 값을 낮춰서 팔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you lower the price to get rid of something quickly.

phrases.en: I will sell my house next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 계획을 말할 때 쓰는 미래형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A future form for talking about a plan.

phrases.en: I cleared out the clothes I don't wear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 작은 물건을 없앨 때 '정리하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For small everyday items, 정리하다 sounds more natural.

explain_en: Formal: deal with things you own by selling or throwing away (옷을 처분하다) '팔다' means handing over for money and '버리다' means throwing away. '처분하다' covers both as 'getting rid of', and is often used for bigger things such as houses, cars or stock.

examples.en: Members get a variety of perks.

examples.ko: 예약하신 분들께 무료 음료 특전을 드려요.
examples.en: We give a free-drink perk to those who booked.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 특전으로 포스터를 나눠 줘요.
examples.en: This movie hands out posters as a special bonus.

examples.ko: 먼저 신청하면 특전을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you apply first, you can receive a special benefit.

examples.ko: 앨범을 사면 사진 특전이 같이 와요.
examples.en: If you buy the album, a photo bonus comes with it.
They gave a special benefit to employees who served long.

explain: 특전은 특정한 사람에게만 따로 주어지는 혜택이에요. 회원, 예약자, 팬에게 주는 선물이나 서비스를 말할 때 많이 써요. 누구에게나 주는 '혜택'보다 한정된 사람만 받는다는 느낌이 있어서 '특전' 안내문에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 회원은 여러 가지 특전을 받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Members can receive various special benefits.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혜택을 받는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the view of the person receiving the benefit.

phrases.en: We give a special benefit to those who made a reservation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 회사가 손님에게 정중하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way for a shop or company to speak to customers.

phrases.en: I got a discount coupon as a member perk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구에게 주는 특전인지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the recipient group in front to say who gets it.

explain_en: Neutral extra perk given to members or buyers (회원 특전) 특전 is a benefit given only to certain people. It is used often for gifts or services for members, bookers, or fans. Compared with 혜택, which anyone may get, 특전 has a limited-recipient feel and often appears in promotional notices.

examples.en: The government collects taxes based on income.
The city hall is collecting parking fees.
The club collected dues every month.
The tax office is in charge of collecting taxes.

examples.ko: 벌금을 징수할 때는 영수증을 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When collecting a fine, you must give a receipt.

examples.ko: 새 제도가 생겨서 요금을 따로 징수하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Under the new system, they decided to charge the fee separately.

explain: '징수하다'는 국가나 단체가 세금, 요금을 걷을 때 써요. 돈을 내는 사람은 '납부하다'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 친구들끼리 돈을 모을 때는 '걷다', '모으다'라고 말하고 '징수하다'는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 은행이 돈을 보낼 때 수수료를 징수해요.
phrases.en: The bank collects a fee when you send money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이나 회사가 서비스 값으로 정해진 돈을 걷을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an organization collects a set fee for a service.

phrases.en: This road collects a toll.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 지나가는 차에게 요금을 걷을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for collecting tolls from passing cars.

phrases.example: 세금 징수는 매년 같은 달에 해요.
phrases.en: Tax collection happens in the same month every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '징수하다'를 명사로 바꾼 말로, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form, often seen in the news.

explain_en: Government or body collecting taxes, fines, fees (세금 징수) '징수하다' is used when a state or organization collects taxes or fees. The person who pays uses '납부하다', so the two pair up. Friends gathering money say '걷다' or '모으다', never '징수하다'.

t90.ax: The club collected dues every month.

examples.en: The thief was arrested last night.
That person was arrested by the police.
They say the arrested man admitted the facts.
If the criminal is arrested, it will be on the news.
He ended up being arrested while running away.
The arrest scene was caught on video.

explain: '잡히다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '체포되다'는 경찰이 법에 따라 잡았을 때 써요. 그래서 뉴스에서 자주 들어요. '경찰에게 체포되다'처럼 '에게'를 써요. 잡은 경찰 쪽 말은 '체포하다'예요.

phrases.en: The arrested person went straight to the police station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체포를 당한 사람을 가리킬 때 쓰는 꾸밈 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This modifier form refers to a person who has been arrested.

phrases.en: The thief was arrested on the spot in front of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범죄가 일어난 자리에서 바로 잡혔을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when someone is caught right at the place the crime happened.
phrases.en_equiv: to be arrested on the spot

phrases.en: That person has not been arrested yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 잡히지 않았다는 뜻을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say that someone has not been caught yet.

explain_en: Passive, neutral and formal: a person gets arrested (도둑이 체포되다) '잡히다' is everyday, while '체포되다' is for when the police catch someone under the law, so you hear it often in the news. It takes '에게', as in '경찰에게 체포되다'. The police side uses '체포하다'.

gh: be caught by police, news style

p.n: 체포당하다 adds a feeling that the arrest was unwanted or unfair.

t90.ax: The thief was arrested last night.

examples.ko: 정부는 소상공인을 위한 세금 특례를 마련했어요.
examples.en: The government prepared a special tax provision for small business owners.

examples.ko: 이 제도는 일부 지역에만 특례가 적용돼요.
examples.en: A special exception applies only to some regions under this system.

examples.ko: 특례 입학으로 대학에 들어간 학생도 있어요.
examples.en: Some students entered university through special admission.

examples.ko: 시험 특례는 신청서를 내야 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get a special accommodation for the exam only if you submit an application.

examples.ko: 회사가 이번 한 번만 특례로 인정해 줬어요.
examples.en: The company approved it as a special exception just this once.

examples.ko: 특례를 자꾸 만들면 규칙의 의미가 없어져요.
examples.en: If you keep making special exceptions, the rule loses its meaning.

explain: '예외'와 비슷하지만, '특례'는 법이나 제도에서 특별히 따로 정해 둔 규정을 말할 때가 많아요. 그래서 '특례법', '특례 입학'처럼 공적인 말에 잘 나와요. '이번만 봐줄게요' 같은 가벼운 뜻으로는 '예외'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The new special act starts next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별한 경우를 따로 정한 법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A law that sets special rules for particular cases.

phrases.example: 외국에서 오래 산 학생은 특례 입학을 신청할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Students who lived abroad long can apply for special admission.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 조건을 가진 사람에게 다른 방식으로 입학을 허락하는 제도예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A system admitting people with set conditions by a different path.

phrases.en: A special exception applies in this case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별 규정을 실제로 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means actually applying the special rule.

explain_en: Officially granted special treatment or provision, formal (특례 적용) It is similar to '예외' (exception), but '특례' often refers to a rule specially set apart in a law or system. That is why it appears in official terms like '특례법' and '특례 입학'. For a casual 'I'll let it slide this time', '예외' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: Some students entered university through special admission.
